subtitle: How a computer learns patterns from data -- and how you tell when it's real.

steps.label: TRADITIONAL PROGRAMMING
steps.sub: A person writes the rules by hand

steps.label: MACHINE LEARNING
steps.sub: Data + known answers -> algorithm finds the rules

eyebrow: A hand-written rule vs. a learned model
code:
def rule_price(sqft):
    if sqft < 1200: return 200
    if sqft < 2200: return 320
    return 450

model = LinearRegression().fit(X, price)
print("rule   :", rule_price(1800))                      # 320
print("learned:", round(model.predict([[1800]])[0], 1))  # 260.8
caption: Someone guessed the rule's thresholds. fit() found the learned model's numbers from data.

code:
print("slope per sq ft:", round(model.coef_[0], 3))   # 0.119
print("intercept:", round(model.intercept_, 1))        # 45.8
caption: Close to the real pattern used to generate the data (0.12, 50) -- recovered from noisy examples.
